chains.title: GATA2 binds the ref allele and activates LMO1 in neuroblastoma
chains.cell_type: Neuroblastoma cells, especially adrenergic/MYCN-amplified context; SK-N-SH is the provided expression context

links.claim: The plus-strand ref allele C corresponds to gene-strand G and preserves a GATA motif, whereas the alt allele A corresponds to gene-strand T and a TATA-like sequence. GATA2 is prioritized as a GATA-family factor because ENCODE GATA2 ChIP-seq has a peak containing rs2168101 in SK-N-SH (E07), but this peak does not itself demonstrate allele specificity. QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked because no QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is provided.

The variant lies in EH38E1518342, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, consistent with an active intronic enhancer element. The SCREEN z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not SK-N-SH-specific.
This enhancer is in the LMO1 gene body about 34.9 kb from the TSS, and credible-set L2G mapping supports LMO1 as the likely target gene.
The proposed mechanism occurs in neuroblastoma cells, where LMO1/MYCN biology is documented and GATA2 ChIP-seq occupies this region in SK-N-SH.

The literature supports an allele-level GATA-versus-TATA effect at rs2168101, with the GATA/ref state associated with higher LMO1 and increased neuroblastoma risk or penetrance and the TATA/alt state protective. Attributing this phenotype specifically to GATA2 remains a mechanistic inference, not a directly demonstrated GATA2-dependent effect.

predictions: Allele-specific GATA2 ChIP-qPCR shows stronger GATA2 occupancy on the ref C allele than the alt A allele in SK-N-SH or another relevant neuroblastoma context.
GATA2 knockdown reduces ref-allele-dependent LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression.
The alt allele weakens GATA2-dependent LMO1 regulation and is protective.
falsified_if: Allele-specific GATA2 occupancy at rs2168101 is not detected in SK-N-SH or another relevant neuroblastoma context.
GATA2 knockdown does not reduce ref-allele-dependent LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression.
A linked variant explains the neuroblastoma association after controlling for rs2168101.

chains.title: TBP binds the protective alt allele and reduces LMO1

links.claim: The alt allele A corresponds to gene-strand T and creates a TATA-like sequence, so TBP is predicted to bind the alt allele more strongly than the ref allele. This is inferred from the literature naming a protective TATA allele, not from direct TBP binding evidence. ENCODE TBP ChIP-seq has no peak containing rs2168101 in SK-N-SH, although absence can also mean no TBP experiment in that biosample. QBiC-SELEX coverage is not_checked because no QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is provided.

The variant lies in EH38E1518342, a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal, consistent with an active intronic enhancer element. The SCREEN z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not SK-N-SH-specific.
This enhancer is in the LMO1 gene body about 34.9 kb from the TSS, and credible-set L2G mapping supports LMO1 as the likely target gene.

The proposed TBP/TATA-dependent effect would occur in neuroblastoma cells, where the protective TATA allele has been linked to reduced MYCN-driven tumor penetrance. Direct TBP function in SK-N-SH is not shown.

Alt-allele TBP binding is proposed to interfere with productive enhancer activity and reduce LMO1 expression, lowering neuroblastoma risk. The literature supports the protective direction of the TATA allele, but not the TBP-specific mechanism.

predictions: TBP or a TATA-box factor occupies the alt A allele more strongly than the ref C allele.
The alt allele reduces LMO1 enhancer activity in neuroblastoma cells.
The alt allele restricts or reduces adrenergic neuroblastoma phenotypes.
falsified_if: TBP or a TATA-box factor does not show preferential alt-allele occupancy at rs2168101.
The alt allele does not reduce LMO1 enhancer activity or LMO1 expression.
GATA-factor binding and function fully explain the allelic effect.

grades_v0.reason: Literature supports a GATA motif at the rs2168101 locus and an allele effect, but does not show GATA2 binding; no QBiC-SELEX or ChIP-seq evidence distinguishes GATA2 from other GATA factors. This is at best an indirect motif-based binding prediction.

E03 directly places the variant in EH38E1518342, a dELS with DNase and H3K27ac signal. The element annotation is supported, although the SCREEN z-scores are maxima across biosamples rather than neuroblastoma-specific.
E02 places the variant in the LMO1 gene body about 34.9 kb from the TSS, and E05 L2G/credible-set evidence supports LMO1 as the target gene. This is sufficient for the gene-link claim.
E06b and E06i support LMO1/MYCN biology in neuroblastoma, but do not show GATA2 expression or function in SK-N-SH or demonstrate the proposed GATA2-dependent mechanism in this cell context.

E06f/E06g support a GATA-allele versus protective TATA-allele effect on neuroblastoma risk/penetrance and LMO1 biology, but the phenotype link over-claims by attributing the effect specifically to GATA2. E04/E05 are dominated by non-neuroblastoma traits and do not establish the GATA2-specific direction.

Literature supports a GATA motif, but there is no evidence that GATA3 is the relevant GATA factor. Selection of GATA3 is not supported by QBiC-SELEX, ChIP-seq, or expression evidence; this remains an indirect motif-based prediction.
E03 directly annotates the variant in EH38E1518342 as a distal enhancer-like cCRE with DNase and H3K27ac signal. The element claim is supported.
E02 and E05 support LMO1 as the local gene and L2G target. The gene-link claim is supported.
Neuroblastoma is a plausible context from E06b/E06i, but GATA3-specific function in SK-N-SH or this element is not shown.

The allele-level GATA/TATA literature supports a risk direction, but the claim specifically requires GATA3-dependent enhancer activity and LMO1 induction, which is not demonstrated. This is an over-claim for GATA3.
E06f/E06g name a protective TATA allele, but do not show TBP binding. The TBP link is inferred from a TATA-like sequence and is not supported by direct binding or QBiC-SELEX data.
E03 directly supports the element annotation as a distal enhancer-like cCRE containing the variant.
E02 and E05 support LMO1 as the local gene and likely target.

The protective TATA allele has been linked to reduced MYCN-driven tumor penetrance in zebrafish (E06g), but the proposed TBP-dependent mechanism in neuroblastoma cells, including SK-N-SH, is not demonstrated.

E06g supports the protective direction of the TATA allele at the phenotype level, but the claim attributes this to alt-allele TBP binding, for which no direct evidence is provided. The TBP-specific mechanism is over-claimed.

grades_final.reason: E03 directly supports the variant's location in EH38E1518342, a dELS with DNase/H3K27ac signal; the claim appropriately notes the z-scores are maxima across biosamples, not SK-N-SH-specific.
E02 places the variant in the LMO1 gene body 34.9 kb from TSS, and E05 gives LMO1 as the top L2G gene; E06f also links the locus to LMO1.
E07 directly shows a GATA2 ChIP-seq peak containing rs2168101 in SK-N-SH, and E06b/E06i support LMO1/MYCN neuroblastoma biology. The cell-type claim is appropriately limited.

To better understand this synergy, we performed single-cell RNA sequencing analysis on primary tumors from transgenic zebrafish overexpressing MYCN alone or with LMO1.

Our data suggest that LMO1 overexpression in MYCN-amplified NB cells increases the pro-metastatic properties of macrophages in the tumor-cell microenvironment, which is important for driving NB metastasis.
We found LMO1 rs2168101 G > T and rs11603024 C > T as well as LMO2 rs7933499 G > A were significantly associated with Wilms tumor risk.

Stratified analysis demonstrated a protective role of rs2168101 GT/TT genotypes against Wilms tumor in the subgroups of age ≤ 18 months, males and clinical stages I/II compared to the rs2168101 GG genotype.

Fourteen loci, including ten protective polymorphisms from CASC15, BARD1, LMO1, HSD17B12, and HACE1, and four risk variants from BARD1, RSRC1, CPZ and MMP20 were significantly associated with neuroblastoma risk.
Both LMO1 expression levels and the risk of developing neuroblastoma in children are associated with a single nucleotide polymorphism, G/T, that affects a GATA motif in the first intron of LMO1.

Here, we showed that WT zebrafish with the GATA genotype developed adrenergic neuroblastoma, while knock-in of the protective TATA allele at this locus reduced the penetrance of MYCN-driven tumors, which were restricted to the mesenchymal cell state.
They now demonstrate experimentally, using genome-edited zebrafish, that a polymorphism in the human rs2168101 locus of the LMO1 gene determines which CRC is active in a tumor.

The authors previously showed that overexpression of LIM-domain-only 1 (LMO1), a transcriptional coregulator, synergizes with MYCN to accelerate tumor formation and metastasis in an NBL-zebrafish model.
